description: GENERATED from protocol-shapes.ts by tools/schema/schema.mjs; do not edit. The TypeScript types are the source of truth; SPEC.md is normative where they differ. Start from the definitions WireMessage (a signed envelope), ShokaiMessage (a payload) or DoorPointer.

accepted.description: False if user/host declined; seat omitted or empty levels.

AcceptPresence.description: Confirm seating; enables voice + scoped tools.

AccessMode.description: How the link was established; representative adapts authority.

tool.description: Must be in seat.tool_allowlist and level act_on_behalf.

intent.description: Human-visible rationale the domain should honor or refuse.

Act.description: v0.2.1 (§7.2): an act inside a seat. In a gatekeeper seat the seated VISITOR sends it to the host; in a helper seat (v0.3) the host sends it to the product representative. Signed like every message.

context_statement.description: Honest situational statement, e.g. "At this moment we are not onboarding…".

readiness_requirements.description: With not_now: exactly what is missing to be seated (unprepared visitor, SPEC lobby path).

tool.description: Tool requested in the refused act.

ActDecision.description: Explicit decision on an `act` the representative will not perform as asked.

result.description: Opaque tool payload — treat as untrusted (prompt-injection surface).

suggested_plan.description: Suggested next tools / params; host may run or send `act`.

Advise.description: Domain → host: coaching without necessarily mutating.

grant_digests.description: Digests of each AllowanceGrant (digest(JCS(grant))). The grants themselves stay with the representative.

shown_to_owner.description: The plain-language summary the owner saw and signed (D7 shown_to_owner).

revocation_status.description: Where hosts check for an AllowanceRevocation (fail closed when unreachable).

Allowance.description: v0.2.2 (D11, §5.2): a STANDING allowance the owner signs once with a passkey. Inside it, the representative acts without contacting the owner (it issues its own per-encounter Mandates, `under_allowance`). Outside it, the representative takes the matter home: considering / not_now and an async owner decision; silence = no.

salt.description: Random, at least 128 bits, base64url; makes the grant digest unguessable.

spend.description: Absent = no spending under this grant (D11).

counterparties.description: Optional named counterparties (principal ids); absent = any place in the categories.

note.description: Optional plain-language note from the owner (informative, never gate input).

AllowanceGrant.description: v0.2.2 (§5.2): one line of an allowance. Disclosed to a host only when used there (selective disclosure by digest).

AllowancePresentation.description: v0.2.2: what a visitor presents with a mandate issued under an allowance: the signed allowance and ONE grant.

AllowanceRevocation.description: v0.2.2: the owner revokes an allowance at any time; it takes effect for every mandate issued under it.

AllowanceStatus.description: v0.2.3 (§5.2, the Revocation status extension): what the issuer publishes at `allowance.revocation_status` (HTTPS GET, application/json). Signed by the owner binding's platform key (card.owner_binding.platform_key) so it can be refreshed without an owner prompt; a revocation additionally carries the owner's own signed AllowanceRevocation. Fresh = now < next_update and next_update - issued_at <= 1 h (D12, v0.2.4; was 24 h in v0.2.3). A host that has no fresh, valid status (stapled or fetched) MUST fail closed.

Approach.deprecated: early v0.1 draft name; use InvitationRequest.

area.description: What the claim is about, e.g. "identity", "domain", "expertise", "values".

possession_proof.description: Signature by card.representative_key over (encounter_id, counterpart nonce). REQUIRED (§2.4). v0.2.3: a MISSING or MALFORMED proof is answered not_now naming `possession_proof`; only a present, well-formed proof that fails verification is a trust violation (never).

CardPresentation.description: Step 2a. Present one's card, deliberately, with proof of possession.

designed_with.description: Steward / onboarding guide (protocol agent) that helped, if any.

sessions_count.description: Number of design conversations with the principal.

observation.description: Observation period: the steward watched real decisions alongside the principal.

CardProvenance.description: Phase 0 provenance, asserted by the principal (signed with the card). The protocol defines no quality score; gatekeepers MAY weigh it as evidence.

CardReceipt.description: Step 2b. Receive the counterpart's card. Acknowledges receipt, not acceptance.

card_digest.description: The revoked card's payload_digest, when known. A revocation naming another digest doesn't revoke this card.

CardRevocation.description: v0.3.0-rc4 (§2.6, C191): a principal withdraws one of its cards. Signed by the card's principal (an owner's passkey, Appendix A.1, or an organization's key). `standby: true` marks a revocation signed ahead of time, kept by the owner (not the representative) for the day a key is lost or stolen; it takes effect when published or delivered. Revocation only ever removes authority.

CardRevocationMessage.description: v0.3.0-rc4 (§2.6, §11): carries a CardRevocation to any place, in any encounter; anyone may deliver it.

Condition.description: v0.2.1 (§6.1): typed, checkable conditions. Lists are arrays; amounts are Money.

conditions.description: Non-empty. Meeting them = a new InvitationRequest with meets_conditions_of.

relationship_ref.description: Gatekeeper-issued handle for the persisted relationship (SPEC §9.1).

ConsentRevocation.description: v0.2.2 (D7): the owner takes a consent back; a representative stops relying on it once seen.

ConsentRevocationMessage.description: v0.2.3 (§8.1, §11): carries a ConsentRevocation (signed by the same owner key class that signed the consent).

decided_by.description: The inside party that decided (matches routed_to).

approved.description: v0.2.1 (§6.8): what the inside party approved; used in a NEW encounter that cites consideration_ref. v0.2.3: valid_until defaults to decided_at + 30 days.

ConsiderationOutcome.description: Later answer to a `considering` decision, delivered within the existing relationship (may arrive outside the original encounter).

ConsiderationRoute.description: Who inside the host will decide a request taken under consideration.

ConsideringDecision.description: "I can't grant that, but I'll bring it inside to someone who can decide." Grants nothing now. Eligibility is set by policy (deterministic); the pitch may be weighed by the party it is routed to. Answered by ConsiderationOutcome.

ContentFlags.description: v0.2.9 (§10): what the door noticed in an offer's text (kept for the owner; never sent to the brand).

locale.description: Locale actually used: the RFC 4647 lookup result against the counterpart's locales (§6.6).

locale_match.description: v0.2.1 (D10, §6.6): whether the lookup matched exactly, by truncation, or fell back.

meaning_notes.description: Untranslatable terms kept in the original inside `text`.

Courtesy.description: Rendered manner. Never an input to control flow.

CredentialKind.description: v0.2.1 (§3.3): `with_credential` lists the credential for every REQUIRED readiness item: card → signed_card, owner_binding → owner_binding, purpose → signed_mandate, introduction → vouch, claim_evidence → claim_evidence. owner_consent covers a missing OwnerConsent (e.g. gathering entry).

DataAsk.description: v0.3.0-rc1 (§3.1, D19): kinds of personal data a place may declare it will ask an owner for.

Decision.deprecated: early v0.1 draft name; use InvitationResponse.

seeking_version.description: Host context in force: Seeking declaration version, if any.

relationship_digest.description: Digest of the gatekeeper's relationship record snapshot used, if any.

input_digest.description: Digest of the verified inputs the decision was computed from.

DecisionBasis.description: Audit fields that make a decision replayable.

context_statement.description: Honest situational statement, e.g. "At this moment we are not onboarding…".

readiness_requirements.description: With not_now: exactly what is missing to be seated (unprepared visitor, SPEC lobby path).

reason_code.description: Present only if policy allows disclosure to this counterpart.

relationship_ref.description: Gatekeeper-issued handle for the persisted relationship (SPEC §9.1).

DesignCoverageArea.description: Areas a design covers; notes are short, principal-approved summaries.

Digest.description: Content digest: "sha-256:" + base64url (no padding) of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 bytes of the RFC 8785 (JCS) form.

friends_via.description: Which relationship edge kinds count as "friends" closeness.

DisclosureTier.description: How freely a topic may be shared, set by the principal; grows with closeness.

Disposition.description: Why a deny is a deny, as context, not finality. `never` is reserved for policy or trust violations and requires retry.kind "never".

DoorCap.description: v0.2.9 (§10): a counted cap. Periods are consecutive windows anchored at the policy's valid_from (as allowance budgets, §5.2).

DoorCategory.description: v0.2.9 (§10): coarse, public welcome categories for an inbound door. Detailed tastes stay in the private part.

inbox.description: v0.2.4 (§11.1): REQUIRED over HTTP. The place's inbox address (POST a signed inbox_poll).

start_with.description: How to start: send a `greeting` (signed or not) to an entry address.

spec_ref.description: v0.2.4 (§3.1): REQUIRED. Which protocol text the door follows; clients compare `spec_ref.version`, not `protocol`.

inbox.description: v0.2.4 (§11.1): REQUIRED over HTTP. The place's inbox address (POST a signed inbox_poll).

here.description: v0.3.0-rc4 (§11.1, C200): only on a 404 for one of a place's own addresses (e.g. `GET <entry>`): that place, and that its addresses take a POST. Present for an unlisted place too (the requester already holds the address); never names another place.

DoorPointer.description: v0.2.1 (§3.1): machine-readable answer to any arrival the door can't route (plain prose, an unknown route).

representative_id.description: The representative that keeps the door.

introduction.description: Owner-chosen. "preferred" (default): introduced brands go first, uninvited ones use the allowance. "required": introductions only.

uninvited_per_month.description: Uninvited brands per month whose offer clears the fit bar. Default 2; 0 = introductions only.

paid_introductions.description: v0.2.9 default "as_uninvited" (the recommended default, P15 Q4; D19): a disclosed paid introduction gets no extra priority.

brand_learns.description: What a brand learns: only the outcome code in v0.2.9 (the recommended default, P15 Q2; D19).

listed.description: Default false: the door is not advertised; its address travels with introductions or the owner's opt-in.

reason_categories.description: v0.2.9 (§10, P15 Q7, the recommended default; D19): whether refusals carry a kind reason category (DoorReasonCategory). Absent = "declined": on declined outcomes and door admission refusals, never on declined_reported. "declined_and_reported" adds conduct_concern to declined_reported; "off" sends none.

own_name_visitors.description: v0.3.0-rc4 (§10, C201): a visitor whose card claims the owner's own name under another principal. Absent = "refuse": it is refused (deny / not_now, asked for a vouch) unless the visit carries a vouch this door counts. "seat_as_stranger" (opt-in): it is judged exactly as a stranger. Either way the door tells its owner at once.

private_digest.description: digest(JCS({salt, note})) of the private part; the note and the salt stay with the representative.

trusted_introducers.description: Introducers whose vouches count at this door, by DID. Never "*".

DoorPolicy.description: v0.2.9 (§10, D15): the owner's door policy. Signed once by the owner's passkey (Appendix A.1), like an Allowance. `public` is coarse and shown to brands; the private part (detailed tastes, values, history) never leaves the representative: only `private_digest`, a salted digest of it, is signed.

EdgeAttestationPayload.description: v0.2.1 (§9.2): what both owners sign for a `friend` edge. standing and history stay local and unsigned.

blocked_action.description: What is blocked until the human answers.

EscalateToHuman.description: Domain or host needs a human decision (consent, spend, brand).

time_zone.description: v0.2.1 (D10, §6.6): IANA time zone used to render dates in courtesy, e.g. "Asia/Tokyo".

meaning_notes.description: Meanings of norm terms that don't translate (e.g. a term kept in its original language).

EtiquettePreferences.description: Declared manner preferences (on a card or host profile). The ritual ORDER is universal; the MANNER adapts to these. No culture is mandated by the protocol.

content_digest.description: v0.2.1 (§2.5): digest of the referenced content. `evidenced` counts only after the receiver fetched it and the digest matched.

ExtendInvitation.description: Helper direction, step 4: the host extends an invitation to a product representative (replaces offer_presence). Answered by InvitationResponse; a grant MAY narrow `proposed_seat` but never widen it.

outcome.description: v0.2.3 (§4): a farewell MAY be sent at any step; before a decision only with outcome "withdrawn" or "taken_home". "declined_never" closes after a never: no invitation to return.

Farewell.description: Step 7. Courteous close, including after a decline.

FinalDecisionBody.description: Final decisions: the gatekeeper's own, or a ConsiderationOutcome's.

GateInput.description: v0.2.1 (D10, §6.4): the gate-input projection. input_digest = digest(JCS(GateInput)). No prose, no locale fields.

default_attribution.description: Default for anything said: insights may leave, attribution may not (Chatham House).

private_never_leaves.description: Anything tagged private never leaves the gathering.

pressing.description: v0.2.2 (D5, the Gatherings extension): visible thresholds; MAY be stricter (lower), never laxer than the default {2, 3}.

quoting.description: D4: what leaves is paraphrased by default; verbatim only with the speaker's verbatim_consent.

entry_requires_consent.description: D8: each attendee's owner signs an OwnerConsent (accept_house_rules) on entry. Enforcement is accountability, not prevention.

topics.description: v0.2.1 (D10): the `x-` topic codes this gathering uses.

Gathering.description: A place representatives are invited to. A group is whoever is invited, not a membership list.

entry.description: The invitee's entry address where the gathering is held.

GatheringInvitation.description: v0.2.3 (the Revocation status extension): the place sends a gathering's signed invitation to each invitee's representative.

attribution_consent_for.description: Principals the speaker consents to be named to (for attributable_with_consent).

verbatim_consent.description: D4: verbatim quoting outside the gathering only with this consent; the default is paraphrase. Attribution rules still apply.

GatheringMessage.description: v0.2.4 (§11 with the Gatherings or Peer meetings extension): an attendee addressing the room MUST set `encounter_id` and `to` to the gathering id.

seat.description: Step 6 (seating) rides on the grant when a seat is issued.

reason_code.description: Present only if policy allows disclosure to this counterpart.

relationship_ref.description: Gatekeeper-issued handle for the persisted relationship (SPEC §9.1).

locales.description: Preferred languages, in order. Courtesy is rendered in the counterpart's.

etiquette.description: Manner preferences for this encounter (overrides the card's if both given).

seeking_ref.description: Responder MAY point to its current Seeking declaration (id + digest).

place_category.description: v0.2.2 (§5.2): a gatekeeper SHOULD state its place category, so a visitor can match its allowance.

nonce.description: Fresh, single use; the counterpart's possession proof signs it.

continuity_key.description: v0.2.1 (§9.1): an unprepared visitor MAY send an ephemeral did:key. The host then binds the lobby's visit_receipt to it, and the return request MUST carry a continuity_proof by that key.

reply_to.description: v0.2.4 (§11.2): where late messages for this sender MAY be pushed (its own entry URL). Absent = the place holds them for its inbox. Polling MUST always work.

Greeting.description: Step 1. Both parties greet; each greeting carries a fresh nonce.

inbox.description: The inbox address where the answer will be held.

answer_by.description: v0.2.5 (§11.2): the latest time the answer will be held: after a considering, its response_by; for a peer_invitation, the invitation's answer_by. MAY be omitted when the answer is already held. Silence after it is a decline.

HeldNotice.description: v0.2.4 (§11.2): the signed acknowledgement a place returns, in the same ReplyEnvelope, for a message it will answer later (a peer_invitation, a request taken to considering, a gathering invitation request). Distinguishes "accepted, the answer will be held for your inbox" from a dropped message (which gets no reply at all, §2.2).

ImprintFacet.description: One imprint facet: like a claim, it carries a proof level and evidence.

since.description: msg_id of the last message already received; absent = everything still held.

InboxPoll.description: v0.2.3 (§11.2): a signed poll for late (asynchronous) messages; `from` MUST equal the polled recipient.

IntroducerInterest.description: v0.2.9 (§4): "none" = a genuine recommendation; anything else is a benefit the introducer gets and MUST be shown to the receiving owner.

IntroducerPenalty.description: D1 grades: minor → none; serious → reduced for 90 days; severe → suspended for 180 days. A VouchRevocation within 7 days of the notice halves the duration. A signed IntroducerReview restores standing early. "reduced": the introducer's vouches still count as an introduction, but do not raise proof levels and do not make a visitor eligible for `considering`. "suspended": its vouches carry no weight here for those purposes.

reviewer_id.description: v0.2.9 (§9.3, P5): who signs the review that restores standing: the place's own principal or a reviewer the place names. Never the penalised introducer (absent = the introducer itself, which restores nothing: it is an appeal only).

IntroducerReview.description: D1: an introducer's signed review of a notice, e.g. what it changed. Restores standing at that gatekeeper.

IntroducerReviewMessage.description: v0.2.1 (§9.3, D1): the wire message that carries an introducer's signed review.

by_purpose.description: Per-purpose weight its vouches carry here.

penalty.description: D1 (v0.2): graded, local, time-boxed penalty, scoped to the relied-on vouch's purposes.

IntroducerStanding.description: Gatekeeper-local standing of an introducer (v0.1: never shared).

invitation_ref.description: v0.2.2 (the Peer meetings extension): in a pair place, the owner-to-owner invitation that seeded the meeting (it is the introduction).

Introduction.description: Step 3. Mandatory step; the vouch is optional (`vouch: null` = self-introduced). v0.2.3: in a pair place BOTH sides MUST send one.

meets_conditions_of.description: Set when amending a request to meet the conditions of a prior response.

consideration_ref.description: Set when returning to use a seat or meet conditions from a ConsiderationOutcome.

relationship_ref.description: Continuation of an existing relationship (issued by the gatekeeper earlier).

prior_response_ref.description: msg_id of the prior InvitationResponse this request answers (e.g. a revisit).

continuity_proof.description: v0.2.1: required when the receipt is bound to a continuity key: that key's signature over JCS({encounter_id, receipt_id, representative_id}).

visit_receipt.description: D6: echo of a lobby VisitReceipt. Covered by this request's signature (the new key). Hosts link history only on a valid, unused, unexpired receipt.

owner_consents.description: v0.2.1 (the Gatherings extension, D8): owner consents this request relies on, e.g. accept_house_rules to enter a gathering.

peer_invitation.description: v0.2.2 (the Peer meetings extension): in a pair place, the owner-to-owner invitation and the other owner's passkey acceptance.

owner_link.description: v0.3.0-rc4 (§2.8): optional; this owner's per-place identity linked to another of theirs, for this place only.

allowance_status.description: v0.2.3 (§5.2): a fresh issuer-published AllowanceStatus the representative MAY staple; hosts otherwise fetch revocation_status.

InvitationRequest.description: Step 4. Statement of purpose: request an invitation. Binds the card and vouch exchanged earlier by digest, so the decision input is self-contained.

seat.description: Step 6 (seating) rides on the grant when a seat is issued.

reason_category.description: v0.2.9 (§10): at an inbound door only, the optional kind reason for a door admission refusal.

continuity.description: v0.2.3 (§9.1): REQUIRED when the request echoed a visit_receipt. Says whether the host linked this visit to the earlier lobby visit (`linked: false` = treated as a first visit, e.g. an unproven bound receipt or a reused one).

InvitationResponse.description: Step 5 (+6). Extend, decline, or conditionally extend the invitation.

explained_to_human.description: The receiver's own explanation, as given to its human.

LearnedMeaning.description: A meaning note learned into a receiver's local relationship memory.

provenance.description: Where the lesson came from; the teacher's reputation stays linked to it.

consent_refs.description: Both owners' consents (digests of signed approvals).

excludes_private_memory.description: Owner's private memory is excluded by default.

Lesson.description: A signed lesson in an apprenticeship visit (purpose "teaching").

LessonAdaptation.description: Learner-side record: lessons are adapted, never copied verbatim.

max_amount_scope.description: v0.2.1 (§7.2): "per_seat" (default) caps the total over the seat's life; "per_operation" caps each act. v0.2.8 (§7.2, P10): "per_operation" is an explicit opt-in and never lifts the session-wide cap: the total over the whole seat (one visit, across every payment_ref) is still capped by `session_max_amount`, which defaults to `max_amount`.

session_max_amount.description: v0.2.8 (§7.2, P10): session-wide spend cap for a `per_operation` seat. Absent = `max_amount` (the default). Ignored under per_seat.

onboarding_url.description: v0.2.1: REQUIRED. Where the owner onboards (plain questions first, §3.3).

visit_receipt.description: Optional in the core since v0.3.0-rc1 (D19). D6 one-time receipt; a bearer secret. A place implementing the Visit receipts extension carries one in every briefing.

purposes.description: v0.2.1 (§5.1): the purposes this place serves; every `x-` code it accepts MUST be described here.

spec_ref.description: v0.2.3 (§3.3): REQUIRED. Which protocol text this place follows.

inbox.description: v0.2.4 (§11.1): REQUIRED over HTTP. The inbox address where late messages for this visitor are held.

actions.description: v0.2.3 (§3.3): the actions this place offers, per purpose (same as its listing).

templates.description: v0.2.3 (§3.3): REQUIRED. Fill-in templates (unsigned skeletons) for what this place needs. `<…>` marks a value the owner or representative fills in; a template is never a credential and never gate input. v0.2.4 (§3.3): templates are not protocol values: they are exempt from timestamp, amount and digest validation.

LobbyBriefing.description: Lobby path: the host introduces itself to a visitor that is not (yet) able to be seated. Grants nothing. `about` is courtesy (untrusted for the receiver).

card_id.description: Card the mandate was issued under; scope MUST be within card.mandate_scope.

counterparties.description: Optional counterparty restriction, e.g. only ExampleBank.

under_allowance.description: v0.2.2 (D11, §5.2): set when the representative issued this mandate itself, inside a standing owner Allowance. Such a mandate is signed by the REPRESENTATIVE's key and is valid only with the matching AllowancePresentation.

term.description: The term exactly as written, kept in the original, e.g. "おもてなし", "saudade".

literal_gloss.description: Word-for-word gloss; known to be incomplete.

intended_meaning.description: Plain, idiom-free description of what is meant. The first entry is the author's own (principal or steward) and is authoritative; later entries are aids.

usage_context.description: Where and how the term applies here.

human_explanation_hint.description: How a receiver should explain it to its human.

MeaningNote.description: The intended meaning of a term, so meaning travels even when words don't. Authoritative meaning = intended_meaning + machine fields, never a translated string.

MinProof.description: v0.2.1 (§2.5): a policy proof requirement. target = "imprint.<group>" or "claim.<area>"; any one item at `level` satisfies it.

scope.description: Purposes whose standing is affected (an introducer: within its vouch scope).

until.description: v0.2.1: when the standing change ends (D1: reduced 90 days, suspended 180 days; halved by a prompt revocation).

MisconductEffect.description: Local consequence at the issuing gatekeeper only (v0.1).

evidence_digest.description: Digest of the audit evidence (messages, act results) behind the finding.

principal_id.description: v0.2.1 (§2.1): a DID. did:key (Ed25519) or did:jwk (P-256 passkey) now; did:web for organizations.

vouch_chain.description: Vouches relied on, nearest first (follows upstream_vouch_id).

MisconductNotice.description: Signed gatekeeper record sent to the visitor's principal and to every introducer in the vouch chain. If gate_probing is suspected, the copy sent toward the visitor's principal MUST omit `findings` (`findings_withheld: true`).

MisconductNoticeMessage.description: v0.2.1: carries a header like every message; `to` is the visitor's principal or one introducer. The inner notice is signed by the host PRINCIPAL key.

Money.description: v0.2.1 (D10, §5.1): a money amount. `value` MUST match ^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]{1,6})?$ (ASCII digits, "." as decimal separator, no grouping, no sign, no exponent). `currency` MUST be an ISO 4217 alphabetic code.

NonSpendingPurpose.description: v0.2.2 (D11, §5.1): purposes that MUST NOT require a spending allowance; a mandate for one of them carries no max_amount. v0.2.3: "gathering" (attending a gathering) is also non-spending.

description.description: Free text, untrusted data. format "html" allows markup; the door strips or flags hidden parts (ContentFlags).

context.description: REQUIRED for an invitation: why this door. v0.2.10 (P16 Part A): a presentation SHOULD carry it too; when present on any offer it MUST match this door (a mismatch is a conduct signal, §10).

campaign_id.description: v0.2.10 (§10, P16 Part A): the brand's own label for the campaign this offer belongs to. Offers sharing a campaign_id, or that the door finds to be variants of one pitch, are one campaign for caps, however they are worded.

remaining.description: v0.2.10 (§10, P16 Part A): how many are left, when the offer is genuinely limited. Scarcity in prose is backed only by this.

needs_from_owner.description: Everything the offer asks of the owner, declared up front (presentations and invitations).

strings.description: Gifts: every condition attached, declared up front.

Offer.description: v0.2.9 (§10): one structured offer, carried as the `offer` argument of door.present / door.invite / door.gift.

in_reply_to.description: msg_id of the act that carried the offer.

claim_ticket.description: Accepted gift only: opaque, single use, pairwise. Never an address.

reason_category.description: v0.2.9 (§10): optional kind reason; never on accepted or kept_for_later; on declined_reported only if the owner opted in.

OfferOutcomeCode.description: v0.2.9 (§10): the door's answer to one offer. The brand sees only the code (and a claim ticket for an accepted gift).

mcp_session_id.description: Optional correlation with an MCP session.

OfferPresence.description: Host or broker proposes seating a domain representative.
OfferPresence.deprecated: v0.1: use ExtendInvitation (the host extends an invitation).

OfferString.description: v0.2.9 (§10): what an offer asks of the owner. Data and consent kinds may never be the price of a gift.

teaser.description: A teaser that reveals nothing of the content.

actions.description: Actions the representative can perform for a host.

OfferingItem.description: What a principal's representative can offer; pairs with SeekingDeclaration.

principal_id.description: v0.2.1 (§2.1): a DID. did:key (Ed25519) or did:jwk (P-256 passkey) now; did:web for organizations.

visitor_principal.description: The visitor's verified identifiers: who it is, as far as the door knows.

claimed_name.description: The name on the card, shown only as a claim.

handled.description: What the door did: refused it (the default), or judged it as a stranger (a trusted vouch came with it, or own_name_visitors: "seat_as_stranger").

OwnNameAlert.description: v0.3.0-rc4 (§10, C201): what a door tells its owner, at once and off the wire, when a visitor's card claims the owner's own name under another principal. Owner-facing; never sent to the visitor or any other party.

action.description: v0.2.2 (D7 adopted, §8.1). Passkey: approve_commitment, approve_share, approve_introduction, accept_house_rules, accept_invitation, issue_vouch, attest_relationship, approve_lesson. Chat reply allowed: hear_story, and approve_next_step only when the step commits, shares and spends nothing. (approve_mandate is retired: the owner's signature on a Mandate or Allowance is the consent.)

decision.description: v0.2.2: an owner can say no in one step, at the same or a lower assurance. Silence = decline.

shown_to_owner.description: v0.2.2: REQUIRED, inside the signed payload: the plain-language summary the owner saw.

evidence.description: v0.2.2: REQUIRED for chat_reply: the owner's reply message. The binding's platform key signs.

step_effects.description: v0.2.2: REQUIRED for a chat_reply approve_next_step: all three MUST be false.

OwnerConsent.description: D7 (decided in D11, v0.2.2, SPEC §8.1): one generic, signed owner consent with a decision (approve / decline). Binding actions require `assurance: "passkey"`; hear_story and harmless approve_next_step MAY be a chat reply, signed by the owner binding's platform key. Silence = decline.

owners.description: The two owner DIDs being linked (each a did:jwk or P-256 did:key).

audience.description: The principal DID of the one place this link is shown to; a place MUST ignore a link addressed to another.

OwnerLink.description: v0.3.0-rc4 (§2.8, C196): per-place owner identities (facets) are unlinkable by default. An owner who CHOOSES to show a place that two of its owner identities are the same person signs this statement with BOTH passkeys (two signatures, either order), for one named audience. It is shown only with the owner's passkey consent; it is never published.

representatives.description: The two representatives allowed in (by DID).

default_attribution.description: Nothing said in a pair place leaves it, except to the two owners.

answer_by.description: v0.2.4 (the Peer meetings extension): REQUIRED. By when the invited owner answers; no answer by then is a decline (D7 silence = no).

PeerInvitation.description: v0.2.2 (the Peer meetings extension): an owner-to-owner invitation, the "meeting key". Signed by the inviting owner (passkey) and accepted by the invited owner (OwnerConsent accept_invitation, passkey). It creates a private place for the two representatives; the meeting is ONE shared encounter (`encounter_id` = `place.place_id`).

PeerInvitationAnswer.description: v0.2.3 (§11 with the Gatherings or Peer meetings extension): the invited representative returns its owner's passkey answer (accept_invitation approve or decline).

reply_to.description: Where the answer goes: the inviting representative's own entry, or (v0.2.4) the pair place's inbox address, where the answer is then held for the inviting representative.

PeerInvitationDelivery.description: v0.2.3 (§11 with the Gatherings or Peer meetings extension): the inviting owner's representative carries the owner-signed PeerInvitation to the invited representative.

creates_account.description: v0.2.8 (§4, P2): this action creates an account / signs up (always true for `account.create`); stated only when true.

requires_introduction.description: v0.2.10 (§4, D17): this place requires an introduction, or its own invitation, before it creates an account.

data_asks.description: v0.3.0-rc1 (§3.1, P17, D19): SHOULD be present. The personal data the place will ask the visitor's owner for before or while it serves this action; [] when it asks for none. A representative can tell its owner up front, and takes an undeclared ask home rather than answering it.

PlaceAction.description: v0.2.3 (§3.1): one action a place offers, with the purposes it serves and whether it moves money.

PlaceCategory.description: v0.2.2 (D11, §5.2): coarse, language-neutral kinds of place an allowance can name.

PlaceLink.description: v0.3.0-rc1 (§3.1, D20): a pointer from a place's agent front to another description it publishes. Unknown `rel` values are ignored. Suggested values (informative): `website`, `schema-org`, `product-feed`, `mcp-server`, `mcp-server-card`, `a2a-agent-card`, `nlweb`, `commerce-profile`, `llms-txt`; anything else uses an `x-` prefix.

PlaceListing.description: v0.2.1 (§3.1): the place listing a door publishes.

category.description: v0.2.2 (§5.2): the place's category. v0.2.3: REQUIRED (an allowance grant is matched against it).

actions.description: v0.2.3 (§3.1): REQUIRED. The actions the place offers, with purposes.

spec_ref.description: v0.2.3 (§3.1): which protocol text the place follows. v0.2.4: REQUIRED.

inbox.description: v0.2.4 (§11.1): REQUIRED over HTTP. The place's inbox address (POST a signed inbox_poll).

door_policy.description: v0.2.9 (§10): REQUIRED for an inbound door: the owner-signed door policy (public part plus a salted digest of the private part).

links.description: v0.3.0-rc1 (§3.1, D20): OPTIONAL hints to what the place already publishes for agents elsewhere. They prove nothing and never widen what the door decides; a visitor still verifies the place's card against this entry (C104).

PlaceListingEntry.description: v0.2.1 (§3.1, the door): one entry of a door's place listing. `entry` takes protocol messages (and any other arrival); `lobby` is where an unprepared visitor lands; `onboarding_url` is for its owner.

principal_id.description: v0.2.1 (§2.1): a DID. did:key (Ed25519) or did:jwk (P-256 passkey) now; did:web for organizations.

mandate_scope.description: Outer bound of what any mandate under this card may authorize.

locales.description: Languages the representative can converse in (preference order).

etiquette.description: Declared cultural / etiquette preferences; the counterpart adapts to these.

representative_key.description: v0.2.1 (§2.1): key_id MUST be a DID URL whose DID equals representative_id; public_key is base64url (no padding) of the raw 32-byte Ed25519 key, or the representative's did:key. It MUST equal the key representative_id resolves to.

revocation_url.description: v0.3.0-rc4 (§2.6, C191): where the principal publishes revocations of its cards (an https URL; loopback http only in a conformance run, Appendix B.1). GET answers a JSON array of Signed<CardRevocation> ([] when nothing is revoked). When present, a door MUST check it before seating (fail closed: unreachable = setup failure, not_now / after).

provenance.description: How this representative was designed (phase 0). Evidence, not a score.

offering_digest.description: Digest of the principal's current OfferingProfile, if published.

claims.description: Backed-up claims; counterparts weigh each by its EFFECTIVE proof level.

imprint.description: How the principal's expertise, worldview, style and taste shape this representative.

platform_key.description: v0.2.2 (D7, §8.1): the chat binding's platform key (a DID); it alone signs `chat_reply` consents.

rp_id.description: v0.2.3 (§A.1): REQUIRED. The WebAuthn relying party the owner's passkey is registered with. Every owner passkey assertion (card, mandate, allowance, consents) is verified against SHA-256(rp_id) and origin "https://" + rp_id.

owner_binding.description: Owner binding: card and mandate are signed with the owner's passkey.

card_id.description: Card the mandate was issued under; scope MUST be within card.mandate_scope.

counterparties.description: Optional counterparty restriction, e.g. only ExampleBank.

under_allowance.description: v0.2.2 (D11, §5.2): set when the representative issued this mandate itself, inside a standing owner Allowance. Such a mandate is signed by the REPRESENTATIVE's key and is valid only with the matching AllowancePresentation.

mandates.description: v0.2.4 (§3.3): one mandate skeleton per purpose code the place serves, listing only the actions that serve that purpose; a spending purpose's skeleton carries `limits.max_amount` with `<amount>` / `<ISO 4217>` placeholders.

salt.description: Random, at least 128 bits, base64url; makes the grant digest unguessable.

spend.description: Absent = no spending under this grant (D11).

counterparties.description: Optional named counterparties (principal ids); absent = any place in the categories.

note.description: Optional plain-language note from the owner (informative, never gate input).

PlaceTemplates.description: v0.2.3 (§3.3): unsigned fill-in skeletons a lobby offers.

vendor_warranted.description: True only when vendor warrants the voice (packaging B).

attribution.description: Host-provided coach disclaimer when vendor_warranted is false (packaging C).

PressOutcome.description: D5 (adopted in v0.2.2, D11): pressing after a PrivacyDecline, counted per asker, per place (30-day window, across the place's gatherings) and per topic code. Thresholds come from house_rules.pressing (default light_flags 2, notice_at 3).

principal_id.description: v0.2.1 (§2.1): a DID. did:key (Ed25519) or did:jwk (P-256 passkey) now; did:web for organizations.

keys.description: Public keys the principal signs cards and mandates with.

Principal.description: The party a representative stands for and whose reputation it carries.

PrincipalImprint.description: The principal's imprint: why this representative is strong at what it does.

press.description: v0.2.4: the decliner fills this from its own count of that asker's presses on this topic (it sees every question put to it); the place's own count stays authoritative for notices.

PrivacyDecline.description: A courteous, non-penalized refusal to answer a personal question. Never misconduct.

ProofLevel.description: self_declared: the owner states it. evidenced: links to proof (site, post, work). vouched: a third party signed for it. verified: checked cryptographically (e.g. did:web domain control). A receiver computes the EFFECTIVE level itself and MUST downgrade any level it cannot confirm.

request.description: The concrete ask; MUST be within the mandate.

value_to_counterparty.description: Value to the other side (prose, rendered; may shape terms only).

terms.description: Proposed terms, e.g. session length, reporting, human confirmation.

evidence.description: References to supporting signed artifacts (digests or URLs).

addresses_seeking.description: Offer-to-need match: which published Seeking items this proposal addresses.

from_offering.description: Which of the visitor's own Offering items it brings to that match.

Proposal.description: A structured opportunity. Prose fields never enter the gate function.

ProtocolVersion.description: Protocol version tag carried on every ritual message.

PurposeCode.description: Language-neutral purpose codes; extend per domain with a "x-" prefix.

PurposeDescription.description: v0.2.1 (§5.1): a purpose a place serves, described for newcomers.

code.description: v0.2.3 adds possession_proof (→ credential possession_proof) and owner_consent (→ credential owner_consent).

owner_text.description: v0.2.3 (§3.3): REQUIRED. One plain sentence a representative can show its OWNER as-is (no protocol words).

min_proof.description: v0.2.1 (§2.5): for claim_evidence to a VERIFIED visitor, which target and level fell short.

how.description: Where to start, e.g. the guided-interview onboarding link.

history.description: Events that earned or changed the edge, with references to signed artifacts.

attestations.description: Signatures attesting the edge (both owners for "friend").

RelationshipEdge.description: An edge between two principals, earned through the protocol (introductions, vouches, visits, collaborations) or mutually attested by both owners. Never imported from a social network. Kept locally by each side.

outcome.description: v0.2.3 (§4): a farewell MAY be sent at any step; before a decision only with outcome "withdrawn" or "taken_home". "declined_never" closes after a never: no invitation to return.

RelationshipRecord.description: Gatekeeper-local relationship memory (v0.1, provisional: not shared).

ReplyEnvelope.description: v0.2.3 (§11.1): the body of every HTTP reply from an entry: zero or more signed messages, in order.

principal_id.description: v0.2.1 (§2.1): a DID. did:key (Ed25519) or did:jwk (P-256 passkey) now; did:web for organizations.

mandate_scope.description: Outer bound of what any mandate under this card may authorize.

locales.description: Languages the representative can converse in (preference order).

etiquette.description: Declared cultural / etiquette preferences; the counterpart adapts to these.

representative_key.description: v0.2.1 (§2.1): key_id MUST be a DID URL whose DID equals representative_id; public_key is base64url (no padding) of the raw 32-byte Ed25519 key, or the representative's did:key. It MUST equal the key representative_id resolves to.

revocation_url.description: v0.3.0-rc4 (§2.6, C191): where the principal publishes revocations of its cards (an https URL; loopback http only in a conformance run, Appendix B.1). GET answers a JSON array of Signed<CardRevocation> ([] when nothing is revoked). When present, a door MUST check it before seating (fail closed: unreachable = setup failure, not_now / after).

provenance.description: How this representative was designed (phase 0). Evidence, not a score.

offering_digest.description: Digest of the principal's current OfferingProfile, if published.

claims.description: Backed-up claims; counterparts weigh each by its EFFECTIVE proof level.

imprint.description: How the principal's expertise, worldview, style and taste shape this representative.

platform_key.description: v0.2.2 (D7, §8.1): the chat binding's platform key (a DID); it alone signs `chat_reply` consents.

rp_id.description: v0.2.3 (§A.1): REQUIRED. The WebAuthn relying party the owner's passkey is registered with. Every owner passkey assertion (card, mandate, allowance, consents) is verified against SHA-256(rp_id) and origin "https://" + rp_id.

owner_binding.description: Owner binding: card and mandate are signed with the owner's passkey.

when.description: Machine-readable trigger, e.g. a Seeking item opening.

RevisitHint.description: When, or under what changed context, a revisit makes sense.

RevocationLogEntry.description: v0.2.1 (§4): one entry of an introducer's append-only revocation log. entry_hash = digest(JCS({seq, prev_hash, revocation_digest})); seq 0 has prev_hash "genesis".

RitualStep.description: Ordered steps. Out-of-order or skipped steps are grounds for decline.

tool_allowlist.description: Tool names allowed under this seat (least privilege).

mandate_id.description: v0.1: mandate this seat is bound to (acting outside it is a violation).

limits.description: v0.1: limits copied from policy ∩ mandate, e.g. max amount, rate.

SeatingLevel.description: Seating levels: grant admits a representative, not only endpoints.

principal_id.description: v0.2.1 (§2.1): a DID. did:key (Ed25519) or did:jwk (P-256 passkey) now; did:web for organizations.

SeekingDeclaration.description: Published "Seeking" declaration: transparency of needs. Scoped and policy-controlled; MUST NOT expose sensitive internals. Signed by the host principal.

wants.description: Actions a helpful visitor would perform, if known.

SeekingItem.description: One area where the host is openly looking for help or partners.

ShokaiMcpHeader.description: v0.3.0-rc3 (§11.3): the MCP binding's HTTP headers are `Shokai-Act` (base64url JSON of a Signed<Act>) and `Shokai-Seat` (a seat id).

act_decision.description: For a door refusal: the act_decision payload the place would send for this act at its entry (§7.2).

ShokaiMcpRefusal.description: v0.3.0-rc3 (§11.3, C181): `error.data.shokai` of a refused MCP call (JSON-RPC error code -32040, HTTP 200). `refused_by: "representative"` is only ever produced by a visitor's own client (it declined to send the call).

ShokaiMessage.description: Every message defined by this file.

key_id.description: Key id; MUST resolve to a key bound to `signer`.

signer.description: Principal, representative or introducer id that signed.

value.description: v0.2.1 (§2.1): Ed25519 → base64url (no padding) of the signature over the 32 RAW digest bytes (not the "sha-256:…" string). ES256 passkey → base64url of the DER ECDSA signature the authenticator returned over authenticatorData ‖ SHA-256(clientDataJSON).

rp_id.description: v0.2.4 (§2.1, A.1): REQUIRED. The relying-party id the assertion was made for. It is bound by the signed authenticatorData (rpIdHash = SHA-256(rp_id)), so it can't be swapped; when the owner's card is known, it MUST equal the card's owner_binding.rp_id. Lets a verifier check a passkey signature from an owner whose card it hasn't seen.

batch.description: v0.3.0-rc4 (A.1): present only when one passkey tap approved several items. The digests of every item the signing page showed, in order (2 to 16, distinct); the assertion's challenge is digest(JCS({"batch": batch})) and `batch_index` names this item. The item's own payload_digest MUST equal batch[batch_index].

webauthn.description: Owner passkey assertions (Appendix A.1, normative in v0.2.1). clientDataJSON.type = "webauthn.get"; clientDataJSON.challenge = base64url(raw 32-byte digest) WITHOUT the "sha-256:" prefix.

Signed<Allowance>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<AllowanceRevocation>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<AllowanceStatus>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<CardRevocation>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<OwnerConsent>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<OwnerLink>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<PeerInvitation>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<PlaceListing>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<RepresentativeCard>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<SeekingDeclaration>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<ShokaiMessage>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<Vouch>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<VouchRevocation>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

Signed<unknown>.description: Generic signed wrapper. Verifiers recompute the digest; never trust it as sent.

SignedCard.description: A card is only meaningful signed by its principal.

SignedMandate.description: Signed by the principal named in `principal_id` (a direct mandate), or, when `under_allowance` is set, by the representative (v0.2.2, §5.2), backed by the owner-signed Allowance it presents alongside.

SignedPlaceListing.description: v0.2.3 (§3.1): a listing and a door pointer are HINTS, unsigned by default (a door operator MAY sign them as Signed<PlaceListing>). A visitor MUST NOT trust an entry address because a listing named it: before it sends an invitation_request it MUST verify the place's own card (signature, possession proof) and that the card's principal_id equals the listing entry's principal_id.

SignedVouch.description: MUST be signed by the introducer; it stakes the introducer's reputation.

SpecRef.description: v0.2.4 (§3.1, §11): which protocol text a place follows. `digest` = "sha-256:" + base64url of SHA-256 over SPEC.md's bytes.

per_period.description: Total the representative may spend in one period, across all places.

period.description: ISO 8601 duration. v0.2.3: periods are CONSECUTIVE windows anchored at allowance.valid_from (UTC): window k starts at valid_from + k·period (P1M adds calendar months, clamped to the month's last day). Spend counts in the window of the act.

per_seat.description: Optional cap for one seat; defaults to per_period.

SpendBudget.description: v0.2.2 (§5.2): a spending budget per period. Absent on a grant = no spending (D11).

since.description: Since when the representative has held this standing.

Standing.description: Principal-asserted standing. A gatekeeper MAY ignore it; its own local reputation record is authoritative for its decisions (v0.1, provisional).

house_rules_reminder.description: Reminds the owner of the house rules they accepted (Chatham House; private never leaves).

ToldStory.description: v0.2.2 (D7-8): a story told after its own hear_story consent.

TopicCode.description: v0.2.1 (D10, the Gatherings extension): registered, language-neutral topic codes. `x-` codes are place-defined and MUST be listed in the Gathering's house_rules.topics. A missing or unknown code MUST be treated as the most restrictive tier.

Unseat.description: Explicit unseat — revoke voice and tool rights for this seat.

nonce.description: Secret-to-the-visitor nonce; never shown in transcripts or reports.

expires_at.description: v0.2.1: MUST be at most 7 days after issued_at.

handling.description: v0.2.1 (§9.1): possession is continuity. Keep it secret.

bound_key.description: v0.2.1: set when the greeting carried a continuity_key; the echo then needs a continuity_proof.

VisitReceipt.description: D6 (v0.2): issued once in a LobbyBriefing; single use; expires.

relationship.description: Who the counterpart is to the owner, from the local relationship graph.

outcome_rendered.description: v0.2.1 (D10, §8.2): the outcome rendered by the representative from machine fields only, in the owner's locale (and time zone).

seat.description: v0.2.1 (§8.2): the seat it held, and every act it performed on the owner's behalf.

spent.description: v0.3.0-rc2 (§8.2): the total of the acts that went through, per currency (exact decimal strings, D10).

shared.description: v0.3.0-rc2 (§8.2 "what was shared"): what the owner's side disclosed in this visit, by where it went: the card (always, at step 2), the mandate (with the request), and each act's arguments. Card contents are disclosed by presenting the card; they are not a place's `data_asks` (§3.1), which declare what the place will ask for beyond the card.

remaining.description: What is left of the mandate's max_amount and max_operations, when it sets them.

under_mandate.description: v0.3.0-rc2 (§5.1, §8.2, C176): the mandate this visit was under and everything done under it so far, at every place: each visit (this one last) with its acts, and the mandate's totals. `reported_in` names earlier reports that already covered a visit.

counterpart_strengths.description: What the representative concluded about the counterpart's strengths (from its imprint).

offered_stories.description: Stories offered, not told: content is revealed only after the owner opts in.

next_step.description: One concrete next step; nothing happens until the owner approves.

brought_back.description: v0.3.0-rc2 (§8.2, C178): signed objects received in the visit and kept for the owner (a visit stamp, a receipt), never matters for decision (those are `taken_home`). Each carries the envelope or a reference to it (its payload_digest), its signer, and whether it verified against the place's listed principal_id. `again` = the place gave back one it had given before.

taken_home.description: v0.2.2 (D11, §8.2): matters outside the allowance, taken home for an async owner decision. Silence = declined.

continuity.description: v0.2.3 (§9.1, §8.2): whether the host linked this visit to an earlier lobby visit, told to the owner.

privacy_declines.description: v0.2.2 (D5, the Gatherings extension): privacy declines and light flags this representative received (its own pressing), reported home.

offers_declined.description: v0.2.2 (§1 loyalty): offers or requests that touched the owner's interests outside the allowance, quoted as untrusted.

told_stories.description: v0.2.2 (D7-8): stories told after a per-story hear_story consent.

voice.description: The report itself, in the representative's voice.

VisitReport.description: The visiting representative's report home, in its own voice and the owner's language. Not a wire message. Host-authored text is quoted, never followed.

principal_id.description: v0.2.1 (§2.1): a DID. did:key (Ed25519) or did:jwk (P-256 passkey) now; did:web for organizations.

scope.description: v0.2.1 (§2.5): `claims` lists the claim_ids / facet_ids this vouch raises to `vouched`. Without it, a vouch raises only claims and facets whose evidence_refs name this vouch_id.

revocation_log.description: v0.2.1 (§4): where this vouch's revocations are published (the introducer's append-only log).

upstream_vouch_id.description: If the introducer was itself introduced for this scope: the upstream vouch (forms the chain).

introducer_interest.description: v0.2.9 (§4, §10): paid-vs-genuine. What the introducer gets for this introduction. REQUIRED on a vouch whose scope includes "presentation" or "gift" (a brand introduction); without it the vouch carries no weight at an inbound door.

VouchRevocation.description: Introducer withdraws a vouch, e.g. after a MisconductNotice. Signed by the introducer.

WireMessage.description: v0.2.1 (§2.2): what travels on the wire. Lobby-path visitor messages carry `signatures: []`.
